premises.name: Filter.principal
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : Filter α
premises.doc: The principal filter of `s` is the collection of all supersets of `s`.

premises.name: Filter.join
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} (f : Filter (Filter α)) : Filter α
premises.doc: The join of a filter of filters is defined by the relation `s ∈ join f ↔ {t | s ∈ t} ∈ f`.

premises.name: Filter.sInf
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} (s : Set (Filter α)) : Filter α
premises.doc:
Infimum of a set of filters.
This definition is marked as irreducible
so that Lean doesn't try to unfold it when unifying expressions.

premises.name: Filter.comap
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (m : α → β) (f : Filter β) : Filter α
premises.doc:
The inverse map of a filter. A set `s` belongs to `Filter.comap m f` if either of the following
equivalent conditions hold.

1. There exists a set `t ∈ f` such that `m ⁻¹' t ⊆ s`. This is used as a definition.
2. The set `kernImage m s = {y | ∀ x, m x = y → x ∈ s}` belongs to `f`, see `Filter.mem_comap'`.
3. The set `(m '' sᶜ)ᶜ` belongs to `f`, see `Filter.mem_comap_iff_compl` and
   `Filter.compl_mem_comap`.

premises.name: Filter.map
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (m : α → β) (f : Filter α) : Filter β
premises.doc: The forward map of a filter

premises.name: Filter.bind
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter α) (m : α → Filter β) : Filter β
premises.doc:
The monadic bind operation on filter is defined the usual way in terms of `map` and `join`.

Unfortunately, this `bind` does not result in the expected applicative. See `Filter.seq` for the
applicative instance.

premises.name: Filter.seq
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter (α → β)) (g : Filter α) : Filter β
premises.doc: The applicative sequentiation operation. This is not induced by the bind operation.

premises.name: Filter.coprod
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : Filter (α × β)

premises.name: Filter.curry
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : Filter (α × β)
premises.doc:
This filter is characterized by `Filter.eventually_curry_iff`:
`(∀ᶠ (x : α × β) in f.curry g, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, ∀ᶠ (y : β) in g, p (x, y)`. Useful
in adding quantifiers to the middle of `Tendsto`s. See
`hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoUniformlyOnFilter`.

premises.name: Filter.lift
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter α) (g : Set α → Filter β) : Filter β
premises.doc:
A variant on `bind` using a function `g` taking a set instead of a member of `α`.
This is essentially a push-forward along a function mapping each set to a filter.

premises.name: Filter.lift'
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter α) (h : Set α → Set β) : Filter β
premises.doc:
Specialize `lift` to functions `Set α → Set β`. This can be viewed as a generalization of `map`.
This is essentially a push-forward along a function mapping each set to a set.

premises.name: Filter.pi
premises.type: {ι : Type u_3} {α : ι → Type u_4} (f : (i : ι) → Filter (α i)) : Filter ((i : ι) → α i)
premises.doc: The product of an indexed family of filters.

premises.name: TopologicalSpace.mk
premises.type: {X : Type u} (IsOpen : Set X → Prop) (isOpen_univ : IsOpen Set.univ) (isOpen_inter : ∀ (s t : Set X), IsOpen s → IsOpen t → IsOpen (s ∩ t)) (isOpen_sUnion : ∀ (s : Set (Set X)), (∀ t ∈ s, IsOpen t) → IsOpen (⋃₀ s)) : TopologicalSpace X

premises.name: TopologicalSpace.ofClosed
premises.type: {X : Type u} (T : Set (Set X)) (empty_mem : ∅ ∈ T) (sInter_mem : ∀ A ⊆ T, ⋂₀ A ∈ T) (union_mem : ∀ A ∈ T, ∀ B ∈ T, A ∪ B ∈ T) : TopologicalSpace X
premises.doc:
A constructor for topologies by specifying the closed sets,
and showing that they satisfy the appropriate conditions.

premises.name: WithTopology.instTopologicalSpace
premises.type: (X : Type u_1) (t : TopologicalSpace X) : TopologicalSpace (WithTopology X t)

premises.name: TopologicalSpace.coinduced
premises.type: {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace X) : TopologicalSpace Y
premises.doc:
Given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `X`,
the coinduced topology on `Y` is defined such that
`s : Set Y` is open if the preimage of `s` is open.
This is the finest topology that makes `f` continuous.

premises.name: TopologicalSpace.induced
premises.type: {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace Y) : TopologicalSpace X
premises.doc:
Given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `Y`,
the induced topology on `X` is the collection of sets
that are preimages of some open set in `Y`.
This is the coarsest topology that makes `f` continuous.
